sections.h2: Offices behind the Georgetown tax bill
sections.html:
Georgetown sits in Williamson County, so two county-level offices touch every bill. The Williamson Central Appraisal District values each parcel and processes exemptions. The Williamson County Tax Office collects the money for the city, the county and other units that contract with it.

Mail and payments go to 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, TX 78626, and the phone is (512) 943-1601. The office takes cash, checks, money orders and cards. Cards add a 2.15 percent convenience fee (minimum $2.50), and online e-checks carry no vendor fee.

The county also runs a tax transparency site at williamsonpropertytaxes.org, which shows the taxing units on a parcel and the dates of public hearings where rates are set. Taxing units set exemptions and rates. Neither the appraisal district nor the tax office does.

The Georgetown levy for 2026 is $0.363167 for each $100 of taxable value, compared with $0.353000 the year before. The city's notice of public hearing printed that figure as both the proposed rate and the voter-approval rate, with a no-new-revenue rate of $0.362168.

The average homestead taxable value went from $404,662 in 2025 to $390,088 in 2026, and the city's total levy on all properties went from $51,935,169 to $53,967,701. The city held its hearing on August 25, 2026 in Council Chambers at 510 W 9th Street.

This is the city's slice only. Williamson County, the school district that serves your street and any municipal utility or special district add their own rates. County statements for 2026 were planned to go out the week of October 19.

The deadline is January 31, and whatever remains unpaid on February 1 is delinquent. A taxing unit may allow at least 21 days after mailing, so a bill mailed after January 10 can push the delinquency date to the first day of a later month.

The collector charges 6 percent in penalty plus 1 percent in interest starting February 1. Each following month the penalty gains a point until it stands at 12 percent in July, and interest never stops. A unit that retains a collection attorney can also assess a fee, capped at 20 percent.

Calendar for a Georgetown homeowner
WhenWhat to expect
Jan. 1The parcel is valued and the year's lien attaches
About Apr. 1Single-family homestead owners get a notice of appraised value
Apr. 30Last day of the regular homestead filing period
May 15Protest filing deadline, or 30 days after delivery if later
Nov. 30First installment when the bill is paid in two halves
Jan. 31Final day to pay; unpaid balances turn delinquent Feb. 1
June 30Second half of a split bill

Owners who are seniors, have disabilities or are disabled-veteran owners may pay in four parts. A homeowner who falls behind can ask the collector about a payment plan, which some offices stretch to 36 months.

Begin with a residence homestead application with the Williamson Central Appraisal District. The regular filing period runs January 1 through April 30, and a late application can still be filed up to two years after the taxes become delinquent. Owners do not need to reapply each year unless the chief appraiser asks or they move.

  • The online route runs through the district's property search: find the parcel, then click the HS Exemption icon. Paper applications are accepted too.
  • The senior exemption starts in the year an owner turns 65.
  • Homestead land is limited to what the owner keeps for residential use, up to 20 acres, and generally an acre or less.
  • Disabled-veteran owners need a rating of at least 10 percent, and a 100 percent rating or 100 percent unemployability compensation can qualify for a total homestead exemption.
  • A surviving spouse who is 55 or older can take over the school tax ceiling of an owner who held the over-65 exemption.

School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value and add $60,000 for owners who are 65 or older or disabled. A homestead's appraised value may climb no more than 10 percent in a year, a cap that starts the year after the exemption is first granted. If the appraisal looks too high, file a protest by May 15, or within 30 days of delivery if the notice came late.

Georgetown has grown fast. The July 2025 estimate of 106,907 residents sits 58.5 percent over the 67,436 estimate base from April 2020, and the 2010 count was 47,400. The city covers 57.33 square miles of land. Owners occupy 69.5 percent of homes. Middle home value is $429,100 and middle monthly rent is $1,795 for 2020 to 2024. About 26.2 percent of residents are past 65, the age that opens the senior exemptions and the school tax ceiling.

sections.h2: Can I sell while behind on taxes?
sections.html:
Yes. At closing, the escrow officer pays the overdue balance from the seller's funds. Request a full payoff statement from the county tax office, current year included, because the lien attached on January 1 to whoever owned the house then.

If the February deadline is near or the penalty months have begun, a short payment agreement can limit the damage. Penalty and interest can sometimes be waived on a written request, which has to be made before the 181st day after the delinquency date and normally after the tax itself is paid.

  • An heir seeking the homestead on an inherited house brings the appraisal district a sworn statement of ownership interest, the prior owner's death certificate and a utility bill.
  • Rentals and vacant properties receive no homestead relief, so the full rate applies.
  • A worn house with a tax lien still sells, and the lien is paid off at closing.

faqs.q: What is Georgetown's city property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: $0.363167 per $100 of taxable value, up from $0.353000 in 2025. Your school district, the county and any special district charge separate rates on top.

faqs.q: How do I pay the Georgetown tax bill?
faqs.a: Use the Williamson County Tax Office at 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, TX 78626, whether you pay online or by mail. Cards add a 2.15 percent fee with a $2.50 minimum, while e-checks avoid the vendor fee.

faqs.q: Until when can I file a Georgetown homestead application?
faqs.a: April 30 closes the regular filing period. Late applications are still taken for up to two years after the taxes turn delinquent.

faqs.q: How much is the penalty if I miss January 31?
faqs.a: A 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest are added on February 1. The penalty grows a point each month through July, and interest continues to build.

faqs.q: Can heirs get a homestead exemption on an inherited Georgetown house?
faqs.a: Yes, if the heir lives in it as a principal residence. Heirs not named on the recorded deed bring the appraisal district a sworn statement of their interest, the death certificate and a utility bill.
